name: Error Propagation
description: Learn about Error Propagation and its applications in physics.

content.overview: Say you measure the length and width of a rectangle, and both measurements have a little error in them. When you multiply them to get the area, does the error just... disappear? Nope—it carries through into your final answer. That's error propagation: how uncertainty travels through your calculations. {{viz:diagram-01}}
keyPoints: Error propagation = how uncertainty from individual measurements carries into a calculated result {{viz:diagram-02}}
Adding or subtracting quantities → their absolute errors add together
Multiplying or dividing quantities → their relative (percentage) errors add together
Example: rectangle with length 10 cm ± 0.1 cm and width 5 cm ± 0.1 cm gives an area with about ±3% uncertainty
content.whyItMatters: Nothing in real science comes from one clean measurement—results are built by combining several imperfect ones. Understanding error propagation is what lets scientists honestly say how much they trust a final calculated result, instead of pretending the errors just vanished along the way.
